utterances.text: It is based on experience. I see no reason for conducting a study. It would be irrelevant. If one was ever in a position to observe situations like that, then one knows.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, did you conduct any trials yourself to try and establish that dust clouds differ based on the angle of entry of a bullet?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It happened many times in my career, in my practice, but I had more experience with level trajectories and of course, the more horizontal the trajectory, the cloud of dust is -- follows the line of the trajectory and is more level too. I had many such occasions to see.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So you must have something in mind when you say, like, high angle of descent. So if we assume that a zero degrees is a straight vertical downward shot and 90 degrees is a straight horizontal shot that's parallel to the ground, what's a high angle of descent for you? Are we talking about something greater than 45 degrees or greater than 60 degrees? Like, what type of angle of entry can cause those dust clouds to look like they do in that video still?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be precisely the angles of descent you mentioned, between 45 and 60 degrees, if it had come from BSA positions which were in the famous silver building which was divided in half by the VRS and the ABiH then the angle would have been far less. To tell you the truth, I did not make any calculations in that regard but it would not have come at a 45-degree angle. In that case, the trace would follow the trajectory. It would have been closer to the ground and could you see the top of the APC and perhaps it was above that height.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Line 4, it seems that it would not have gone over 45 degrees whereas I seem to have heard it would not have been more than 10 degrees.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, not more than 10 degrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If could you repeat your answer then.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I confirm that I said it would not have been in excess of approximately 10 degrees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Poparic, that UNPROFOR soldiers were on the scene and they were on the scene during the shooting, by the way, and they went to the impact points of the bullets; because you talked about the traces, they went to the impact points of the bullets and they stuck an antenna in the holes on the ground, which had a furrow of about 10 centimetres, to check the angle of entry, and for each of the six holes in the ground, the antenna always pointed to the same spot across the river in SRK-held territory. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was unaware of that piece of information. However, what you explain does not tell me much. It doesn't tell me the angle of the antennae. It would be a very important piece of information because on the other side, as I said, there was an ABiH position as well as VRS positions in the same building. Half of the building went in the hands of one side, the other half in the hands of the other. It would have been far more important to determine the angle of descent and I doubt that it was a small angle. If it had been small, the antennae would have been close to the ground, very close to the ground, and then the question would be how they would be able to orient themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Well, those kind of measurements of actual traces on the ground at the time would be far more accurate measurement than an analysis of dust clouds on a video still 20 years after the fact?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends on the crater. Well, if they could stick the antenna in, it confirms the argument that the hits came at a high angle of descent and that the bullet went into the ground. If it had been a small angle, a sharp angle, it would have just skimmed the earth and no antenna could be placed in. If they were able to place antennae it is an indication that it was at a high angle and that the bullet had gone deep. The trace, the opening, was not dishevelled. At a sharp angle it would resemble the trail of a plough and then there would be nothing to hold the antenna. If the antenna could stand on its own as stated in the report it indicates that the degree of descent was a high one which in turn means it could not have arrived from VRS positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Let's have a look at a document, P2421 and it's the UNPROFOR report on the incident. Now, Your Honours, the original of this document is in French. There is an English translation that doesn't include all of the sketches in the document, and B/C/S as well. If Your Honours wouldn't mind, I would propose to display the French one and the B/C/S one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: So we see the original on the right-hand side. Thank you. And I'd like to go over to page 3 in both of these documents. So you should have on the B/C/S the -- there we go, you should have the tags. You see on the original French.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: They are translated for you, Mr. Poparic, and what you see in this diagram is that the bullet entered the exterior wall of the tram and it passed through the top part of the wheel, which makes the second hole, and then passed through one side of that cone-shaped seat support next to the wall, and then struck the other side of the seat support. And Mr. Poparic, you can see on the right-hand side of the schema, that the line created or you can see the line created by the path of entry and the UNPROFOR officer indicated the angle in mils as 1450. And 1450 in a mils system of 6.000 is the same as an 87-degree angle of entry. So by your own explanation, then, it's impossible that these shots came from the Executive Council building; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is impossible they could have arrived from VRS positions. Otherwise, the angle would have been far smaller. From the Executive Council building --

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: No, sorry. I don't mean to interrupt you but there might be an issue with the transcript. My question to you was: By your own explanation, given this angle, it's impossible that these shots came from the Executive Council building, by your own definition of high angle of descent.

utterances.speaker: MILE POPARIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I discussed the definition of high angle of descent, it had to do with the case when projectiles were falling and creating clouds of dust. That's what I said was a high angle of descent. This angle indicates, however, that the bullet came at an angle which indicates that the bullet could not have been fired from VRS positions. It could have been fired from the Executive Council building, at a lower or higher angle. It doesn't necessarily mean that the same shooter opened fire in all three cases, on the first, second and third streetcar. We never claimed that. However, this kind of fire excludes the possibility of fire coming from across the Miljacka. Not at this angle, a projectile would not have had this angle had it had come from across the Miljacka River and impacting a streetcar.

utterances.speaker: MS. EDGERTON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just looking at the clock, and having done my best, I'd like to indicate to Your Honours I would appreciate some time tomorrow morning to finish with this incident and incident F1 and probably two more tram sniping incidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Before we adjourn, I'd like to issue an oral ruling, on the request to withdraw Exhibits D1098 and D1179, and the request to reclassify Exhibit D3030 which were filed by the accused on the 30th of May, 2013. First, the accused submits that the photograph of Markale I stabiliser admitted at D1098 was already admitted into evidence as Exhibit P1940, and second, that D1179 was first marked for identification and later the same document was fully admitted as D2768. Therefore, the accused requests that D1098 and MFI D1179 be withdrawn. With regard to D3030, the Chamber placed it provisionally under seal pending the parties' agreement as to its status. The accused now requests that it be made public after the parties agreed that there are no Rule 70 restrictions that require that it remain under seal. On 30 May, the Prosecution informed the Chamber that, via e-mail, that it would not respond to the requests. The Chamber has reviewed the three documents and notes that P1940 does not contain the same photograph as D1098. Instead the Chamber notes that it is P1970. Otherwise, the Chamber is satisfied with the accused's submission and instructs the Registry to mark D1098 and MFI D1179 as not admitted and to change the status of D3030 from confidential to public. We will continue tomorrow at 9.00. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 5th day of June 2013, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.47 p.m.,
